default.notes: Short stay ‘C’ visa required (€60 single entry); apply online via AVATS and submit documents to the designated visa office or embassy.

groups.notes: EU freedom of movement — enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without time limit (register residence rights apply after 3 months).
EEA and Swiss citizens enjoy free-movement rights in Ireland — enter with a passport or national ID card and stay without a visa.
Visa-free for up to 90 days — no visa, no ETA, no pre-registration. The immigration officer at the border decides the exact permission granted.

IE.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Irish citizens.

GB.notes: Common Travel Area: British citizens can live, work and travel in Ireland without any visa or permission, and are not subject to routine passport control arriving from the UK — but airlines still require photo ID, and a passport is the safest document to carry.

UA.notes: Ireland removed the visa requirement for Ukrainian citizens as an emergency measure in February 2022, and the waiver has remained in force alongside the EU temporary protection scheme. This is an emergency measure that could be withdrawn — confirm on irishimmigration.ie shortly before travel.

ZA.notes: South African citizens DO need a visa for Ireland — the visa requirement was reintroduced in June 2022, ending the previous visa-free access. Apply for a short stay ‘C’ visa (€60 single entry) via AVATS well before travel.

BW.notes: Ireland reintroduced the visa requirement for Botswana in 2022, ending the previous visa-free access. Apply for a short stay ‘C’ visa via AVATS well before travel.

DM.notes: Ireland introduced a visa requirement for Dominica in July 2024 over concerns about its citizenship-by-investment programme. Apply for a short stay ‘C’ visa via AVATS.

HN.notes: Ireland introduced a visa requirement for Honduras in July 2024, ending the previous visa-free access. Apply for a short stay ‘C’ visa via AVATS.

VU.notes: Ireland introduced a visa requirement for Vanuatu in July 2024 over concerns about its citizenship-by-investment programme. Apply for a short stay ‘C’ visa via AVATS.
